topic: 3 Hidden Engineering Features Inside Commercial Airplane Windows That Keep the Cabin Safe at 35,000 Feet
title: Why Airplane Windows Have Tiny Holes 🤯
false_sentence: Ever thought how that tiny hole balances cabin pressure so the outer glass doesn't shatter?
correct_version: The hole does not balance pressure between the cabin and the outside; it allows the middle pane to vent, ensuring the outer pane bears the pressure load and preventing fogging/condensation.
why: The narration implies the hole is a pressure-balancing valve to prevent shattering, whereas its primary function is to manage pressure differentials between the panes to prevent condensation and ensure the outer pane handles the structural load.
